conventions.convention: U is nonempty, connected, simply connected, second countable, smooth and boundaryless; q is smooth of signature (-,+), with a specified smooth timelike field and orientation; r:U→(0,∞) is smooth.

The sphere has outward area form ω(u,v)=det(p,u,v), while vol_g=-r² ε₂∧ω. Consequently ⋆ε₂=r²ω and ⋆ω=-r⁻²ε₂; electric and magnetic charges are respectively (4π)⁻¹∫⋆F and (4π)⁻¹∫F over outward-oriented orbit spheres.
Rotational invariance means ρ_R* T=T for every R∈SO(3), where ρ_R(y,p)=(y,Rp); the geometry is an explicitly specified local warped product, without a claimed global quotient.

The mathematical field equations are dF=d⋆F=0 and Ric(g)=Λg+2Q(F), with Q_ab=F_ac F_b{}^c−g_ab F_cd F^cd/4. Λ is a real constant; this is a mathematical system rather than an adopted physical postulate.
z=q⁻¹(dr,dr), Q²=q_e²+q_m², and varpi=r(1−z)/2+Q²/(2r)−Λr³/6. In geometric units r, charges and varpi have length units, z is dimensionless, and Λ has inverse-length-squared units.

Local rigidity assumes AC_ω and both dr≠0 and z≠0 throughout the patch. It covers both signs of f=z, excludes null-gradient and constant-radius branches, and asserts neither horizon extension nor global uniqueness.

load_bearing.statement: For an exact spherical Einstein–Maxwell–Λ datum, Ric(g)_AB=Ric(q)_AB−2r⁻¹(∇^q_A dr)_B, Ric(g)_ij=(1−z−rΔ_qr)γ_ij and Ric(g)_Ai=0. The field equations imply ∇^q dr=(Δ_qr)q/2, Δ_qr=(1−z)/r−Λr−Q²/r³, and d varpi=0.

Under the spherical orbit geometry and AC_ω, every smooth rotationally invariant real two-form satisfying dF=d⋆F=0 has unique constant flux parameters q_e,q_m with F=(q_e/r²)ε₂+q_mω; these constants equal the normalized signed electric and magnetic sphere fluxes.
On the stated connected, oriented, time-oriented smooth Lorentzian surface with AC_ω and the displayed connection and curvature conventions, ∇^q ε₂=0 and Ric(q)=S_q q/2.
Defines an exact spherical Einstein–Maxwell–Λ datum, its constant flux parameters, z=q⁻¹(dr,dr), and varpi=r(1−z)/2+Q²/(2r)−Λr³/6, without assuming mass conservation or global geometric properties.

Assuming AC_ω, an exact spherical Einstein–Maxwell–Λ datum on a connected patch with dr and z nowhere zero has constant varpi=m and local coordinates (t,r) giving g=−fdt²+f⁻¹dr²+r²γ and F=−q_e r⁻²dt∧dr+q_mω, where f=1−2m/r+(q_e²+q_m²)/r²−Λr²/3. The lifted ∂_t is Killing with squared norm −f.
